name: JWT parsed without signature verification (none-alg / ParseUnverified)
attack_scenario: Attacker base64-encodes {"alg":"none"} plus {"sub":"admin","role":"admin"} with an empty signature; the server accepts it and grants admin access with no secret required.
negative_test_hint: submit a JWT with header "eyJhbGciOiJub25lIn0" (alg none), admin claims, and an empty signature, and assert the server rejects it

exemplar.noncompliant: token, _, _ := jwt.ParseUnverified(tokenString, claims)   // signature never checked
exemplar.explanation: jwt.ParseUnverified decodes the claims but deliberately skips signature checking, and SigningMethodNone / UnsafeAllowNoneSignatureType treat an alg:none token with an empty signature as valid, so any attacker-forged token is trusted. Always use jwt.Parse with a keyfunc that pins the expected signing method, so only tokens signed with the real secret are accepted.
